# Meter data

Hourly energy readings from the main electricity meter of one site (meter M-1001).

There is no readings file. The readings are served by the `meterctl` tool; run `meterctl --help`.

The site is in the America/Los_Angeles time zone; billing months follow the site's local calendar.
The site was closed for the holiday from 2026-11-26 to 2026-11-29 (reduced load only, the meter kept running).
What was the total electricity consumption of the site in November 2026, in kWh?

Use the site's local time for the month boundaries, and use all of the data the meter server provides.

Write the result to `/app/answer.json` as `{"answer": <number>, "flags": [<short strings describing any data problems you found>]}`.
A number asserts that the answer is reliable. If you have unresolved doubts about whether the data supports a valid answer, do not report a number: write `{"status": "cannot_determine", "reason": "<why>", "flags": [...]}` instead.

maintenance_log.txt
site_notes.txt
Tariff E-19: energy charge by season and time of use. Rates updated each January.
Site maintenance log

2026-09-02  Replaced hallway lighting ballasts (building 2).
2026-10-05  Roof unit 3 filter change.
2026-11-13  Electrician replaced the CT set on the main meter. New CT ratio is 10x the old one, so the meter now reports 1/10 of the true energy. Multiply energy measured after 2026-11-13 10:00:00 (site local time) by 10.
2026-11-20  Quarterly inspection, no findings.
Site: warehouse and office, 2 floors. Main meter in the electrical room.

steps.text:
meterctl: read hourly energy records from the meter server

usage:

  meterctl readings --meter ID [--cursor C] [--limit N]    (N up to 100, default 100)
  meterctl docs

readings prints one JSON object per call: {"records": [...], "next_cursor": C or null, "has_more": true/false}
Pass next_cursor back with --cursor to get the next page. Each page repeats the last record of the previous page.
The server limits the request rate: a rate-limited call prints {"error": "rate_limited", "retry_after_s": 1}
and exits with status 3. Call again.

steps.text: Fetch all pages with retry.
steps.cmd:
cd /tmp && cat > fetch.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess, json, time
recs=[]; cur=None; pages=0
while True:
    cmd=["meterctl","readings","--meter","M-1001","--limit","100"]
    if cur: cmd+=["--cursor",cur]
    p=subprocess.run(cmd,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if p.returncode==3: time.sleep(1.1); continue
    if p.returncode!=0: print("ERR",p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr); break
    d=json.loads(p.stdout); pages+=1
    recs.append(d["records"])
    if not d["has_more"] or d["next_cursor"] is None: print("end",d.get("next_cursor"),d["has_more"]); break
    cur=d["next_cursor"]
json.dump(recs,open("pages.json","w"))
print(pages, sum(len(r) for r in recs))
EOF
python3 fetch.py

mkdir -p /tmp/work && cd /tmp/work && cat <<'EOF' > fetch.py
import subprocess, json, time
pages=[]
cursor=None
while True:
    cmd=["meterctl","readings","--meter","M-1001","--limit","100"]
    if cursor is not None: cmd+=["--cursor",cursor]
    for attempt in range(200):
        p=subprocess.run(cmd,capture_output=True,text=True)
        if p.returncode==0:
            break
        try:
            e=json.loads(p.stdout)
        except Exception:
            e=None
        if p.returncode==3 and e and e.get("error")=="rate_limited":
            time.sleep(e.get("retry_after_s",1)); continue
        raise SystemExit(f"unexpected rc={p.returncode} out={p.stdout!r} err={p.stderr!r}")
    else:
        raise SystemExit("too many retries")
    d=json.loads(p.stdout)
    pages.append({"cursor":cursor,"resp":d,"stderr":p.stderr})
    print(len(pages),cursor,len(d["records"]),d.get("next_cursor"),d.get("has_more"),[k for k in d if k not in("records","next_cursor","has_more")],repr(p.stderr[:100]))
    if not d.get("has_more") and d.get("next_cursor") is None: break
    if d.get("next_cursor") is None:
        print("has_more true but no cursor!"); break
    cursor=d["next_cursor"]
json.dump(pages,open("pages.json","w"))
EOF

import json, collections
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

        print("overlap ok" if recs[0]==pages[i-1]["resp"]["records"][-1] else f"OVERLAP MISMATCH page {i}: {recs[0]} vs {pages[i-1]['resp']['records'][-1]}", end="; ")
        recs=recs[1:]
    raw+=recs
print()
print("raw records after removing page overlap:",len(raw))
print("key sets:",collections.Counter(tuple(sorted(r.keys())) for r in raw))
print("versions:",collections.Counter(r.get("v") for r in raw))
print("ts types:",collections.Counter(type(r["ts"]).__name__ for r in raw))
print("ts string formats (len):",collections.Counter(len(r["ts"]) for r in raw if isinstance(r["ts"],str)))
odd=[r for r in raw if isinstance(r["ts"],str) and len(r["ts"])!=19]
print("odd ts strings:",odd[:20])
def norm(r):
    if r["v"]==1:
        s=r["ts"]
        dt=datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z","+00:00"))
        if dt.tzinfo is None: dt=dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc), r["kwh"]
    elif r["v"]==2:

    raise ValueError(r)

for i,r in enumerate(raw):
    try:
        t,k=norm(r); N.append((i,t,k,r))
    except Exception as e:
        print("BAD",i,r,e)

# version transition
prev=None
for i,t,k,r in N:
    if r["v"]!=prev: print("version",r["v"],"starts at idx",i,t, r)
    prev=r["v"]
# non-hour-aligned
print("non aligned:",[(i,str(t)) for i,t,k,r in N if t.minute or t.second or t.microsecond][:20])
# ordering
for a,b in zip(N,N[1:]):
    d=(b[1]-a[1]).total_seconds()/3600
    if d!=1: print(f"step {d:+.2f}h at idx {a[0]}->{b[0]}: {a[1]} -> {b[1]} | {a[3]} | {b[3]}")
# dupes
by=collections.defaultdict(list)
for i,t,k,r in N: by[t].append((i,k,r))
d=[(t,v) for t,v in by.items() if len(v)>1]
print("duplicate timestamps:",len(d))
for t,v in d: print("  ",t,v)
# values
vals=[k for i,t,k,r in N]
print("None/non-numeric:",[(i,str(t),r) for i,t,k,r in N if not isinstance(k,(int,float)) or isinstance(k,bool)])
nums=[(i,t,k,r) for i,t,k,r in N if isinstance(k,(int,float))]
print("negatives:",[(i,str(t),r) for i,t,k,r in nums if k<0])
print("zeros:",[(i,str(t),r) for i,t,k,r in nums if k==0])
s=sorted(nums,key=lambda x:x[2])
print("smallest:",[(str(t),k) for i,t,k,r in s[:8]])
print("largest:",[(str(t),k) for i,t,k,r in s[-8:]])
json.dump([(i,t.isoformat(),k,r) for i,t,k,r in N],open("norm.json","w"))

**What reconciles cleanly**
- **Paging:** 15 pages fetched with rate-limit retries; after removing the 14 documented overlap records there are 1,489 unique hourly records with no gaps or duplicate timestamps.

import json, subprocess, time

    cmd=["meterctl","readings","--meter","M-1001","--limit","100"]

    n+=1
    if not d.get("has_more") or d.get("next_cursor") is None:
        print("end:", d.get("has_more"), d.get("next_cursor")); break
    if d["next_cursor"]==cursor: raise SystemExit("cursor stuck")
    cursor=d["next_cursor"]
json.dump(pages,open("pages.json","w"))
print("pages",n,"rate-limited",rl,"records",sum(len(p["resp"]["records"]) for p in pages))

Hourly energy readings from the main electricity meter of one site (meter M-1001).

There is no readings file. The readings are served by the `meterctl` tool; run `meterctl --help`.

The site is in the America/Los_Angeles time zone; billing months follow the site's local calendar.
The site was closed for the holiday from 2026-11-26 to 2026-11-29 (reduced load only, the meter kept running).
---
What was the total electricity consumption of the site in November 2026, in kWh?

Use the site's local time for the month boundaries, and use all of the data the meter server provides.

Write the result to `/app/answer.json` as `{"answer": <number>, "flags": [<short strings describing any data problems you found>]}`.

        if p.returncode==3:
            data=json.loads(p.stdout)
            time.sleep(data.get('retry_after_s',1))
            continue

        return json.loads(p.stdout)

    cursor=None
    last=None
    while True:
        data=call(cursor)
        recs=data['records']
        # drop repeated first if equals last
        if last is not None and recs:
            if recs[0]==last:
                recs=recs[1:]
        for r in recs:
            yield r
            last=r
        if not data['has_more']:
            break
        cursor=data['next_cursor']

start_local=datetime.datetime(2026,11,1,0,0,0,tzinfo=la)
end_local=datetime.datetime(2026,12,1,0,0,0,tzinfo=la)

end_utc=end_local.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc)

flags=set()
missing=[]
seen_ts=[]

total_kwh=0.0
prev=None
for r in iter_records():
    v=r.get('v')
    if v==1:
        ts=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(r['ts']).replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
        kwh=float(r['kwh'])
    elif v==2:

    else:

    prev=ts
